speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) what are the factors taken into consideration when deciding whether or not to press charges against persons with disabilities, especially those with less than full mental capacity; and (b) whether the Ministry is able to share on any past case studies to illustrate the above.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will involve a careful weighing of a wide range of factors, including the circumstances of the alleged offence and the person.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This may, in some cases, also involve a referral for treatment at facilities such as the Institute of Mental Health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If the Public Prosecutor decides to charge the person, the Public Prosecutor’s charging and sentencing position may be calibrated to take into account the person’s mental condition or disability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: To illustrate, in a 2020 case, a 21-year-old offender committed offences of theft of an SCDF vehicle, cheating and causing hurt to another person by performing a rash act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: He was diagnosed with Schizoaffective Disorder, a serious form of long-term major mental illness, which contributed to his offending.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Ultimately, the Public Prosecutor’s exercise of discretion as to whether to charge a person, including a person with a mental condition or disability, is a fact-dependent exercise.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am well aware that MinLaw and MHA are already stepping up in terms of awareness and supporting people with disabilities in the prosecution processes and even in Police investigations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But I have still have a lot of families whose children – and some of them are adults now – who committed offences.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They seem to be, at the first instance, very, very worried at the start of the process.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I wonder if the Government can do something to assure the disability community and the families, and also to educate further the Government agencies involved, to assure them that the Government is not heartless and that many of these steps are put in and things will just get better.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are lots of anxieties and worries when their children who have less mental or social capacity commit offences.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And that kind of anxiety is just all over the social media or in writings to us as Members of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But maybe for the assurance of the Members of this House as well as to the public, perhaps, I could repeat some of the efforts that have been put in place in attending to these matters.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Police officers who deal with persons with disabilities during investigations are trained to identify to deal emphatically.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They are also trained to spot the behavioural indicators associated with mental disabilities and to engage them sensitively.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They undergo a mental health awareness course developed by the Agency for Integrated Care for Government agencies to train their staff in managing persons with mental health conditions, including persons with dementia.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This helps the officers become more aware of the signs and symptoms, and guides them in communicating with persons of these conditions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As part of their core skills training, the investigation officers (IOs) learn the protocols to handle persons with mental disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: All these officers also undergo training to continuously shore up their skills.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These programmes ensure the IOs are proficient in required investigation procedures and protocols, including those relating to the handling of persons with mental disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But apart from training, there is also a set of internal standard operating procedures when dealing with persons with mental disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The focus is to accord additional protection to such persons and ensure that they are supported throughout the investigation process.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are some of the areas that we can continue to highlight to the parents who are involved.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They are understandably anxious when these things happen and typically all rationality goes out the window because you are very worried.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this is something we can look into.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will take this back as feedback and see what avenues we can continue to enhance the understanding of this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If there are specific cases, please feel free to refer them to us and we will see how we can assist.
